q: The first, second, and last terms of an arithmetic sequence are $b$, $2b$, and $4b$, respectively. If the sum of the first two terms is $15$, find the sum of the entire arithmetic sequence.
If $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{500}{x^n}=250$, find $x$.
The first $2$ terms of an arithmetic sequence are $a_1=\log_4 3$ and $a_2=\log_4 6$. Evaluate $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{20}a_n$.
Evaluate: $$\sum_{k=2}^{\infty}\frac{2025}{5^k}$$
Find the sum of all even integers between $100$ and $200$, inclusive.

The sum of the first three terms of a geometric sequence is equal to the sum of the first three terms of an arithmetic sequence. The first term of the geometric sequence is $405$. The sum of the first term and the common difference of the arithmetic sequence is $195$. Find all possible common ratios for the geometric sequence.
Evaluate: $$\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}3\left(\frac15\right)^k$$
Find the sum of all positive two-digit multiples of $3$.
Find the sum of the infinite series: $$162+1+54-\frac14+18+\frac1{16}+6-\frac1{64}+\cdots$$
Find the value of $x$ so that $x$, $x+6$, and $x+15$ form a geometric sequence.
Find the 2023rd term ($a_{2023}$) of the sequence defined recursively as $a_1=8$, $a_2=12$, $a_n=2a_{n-1}-a_{n-2}$.
Evaluate: $$\sum_{n=2}^{\infty}\frac{3^{n+1}+4^{n-1}}{5^n}$$
Find $x$ so that $\displaystyle\sum_{n=2}^{\infty}9x^{n-1}=1$.
In an arithmetic sequence the 5th term is $12$ and the 8th term is $-3$. Find the sum of the first $20$ terms of this sequence.

Let $S$ be the sum of the convergent geometric series $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}a_1r^{n-1}$, $a_1\ne0$. Let $S_1$ be the sum obtained by adding up every other term of the series for $S$ beginning with the first term, and $S_2$ be the sum obtained by adding up every other term of the series for $S$ beginning with the second term. If $S_1-S_2=2S$, find the value of $\left(\dfrac{S_2}{S}\right)^3$.
The first $4$ terms of an arithmetic sequence are $a$, $2a$, $b$, and $a-6-b$. What is the 100th term of the sequence?
Given: $64+64x+64x^2+64x^3+\cdots=72$. Find the value of $64-64x+64x^2-64x^3+\cdots$.
Evaluate: $$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}n\left(-\frac56\right)^{n-1}$$
Find the sum of the series $5+9+13+17+21+25+\cdots+101$.

The Koch snowflake is generated by starting with an equilateral triangle, then replacing the middle third of each side with an equilateral triangle, and repeating this indefinitely. If the original equilateral triangle has a side length of $9$, find the perimeter of the 7th figure in the sequence.
Given $\dfrac{a}{b-x}=3+(x-1)+\dfrac{(x-1)^2}{3}+\dfrac{(x-1)^3}{9}+\cdots$, where $-2<x<4$. Find $a+b$.
Find all possible sums for the infinite geometric series with first term $36$ and third term $4$.
Evaluate $$\sum_{k=2}^{4}\left(\sum_{n=1}^{k}(2n+1)\right)$$
The first and second terms of an arithmetic series are $200$ and $197.5$, respectively. Let $S_n$ be the sum of the first $n$ terms of this series. What is the largest value of $S_n$?
$3x$, $x-2$, and $x+7$ are consecutive terms of an arithmetic sequence. Find $x$.
The sum of the first $k$ terms of the sequence $2, 6, 18, \dots$ is $19{,}682$. Find $k$.
A ball is dropped from a height of $10$ feet. Each time it hits the ground, it rebounds $\dfrac34$ of the distance it has fallen. How far (in feet) will the ball travel before coming to rest?
Evaluate: $4\times2\times\sqrt[4]{4}\times\sqrt[8]{4}\times\sqrt[16]{4}\times\sqrt[32]{4}\times\cdots$

Given a 4-term sequence such that the first $3$ terms form an arithmetic sequence and the last $3$ terms form a geometric sequence. If the first term is $2$ and the last term is $9$, find the third term of this sequence.
Evaluate: $$\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}1024\left(\frac14\right)^{k-1}$$
$100$ is the first term and $-\dfrac{108}{5}$ is the fourth term of a geometric sequence. Find the second and fifth terms of the sequence. (Answer: second, fifth)
If $\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{n}(2k+1)=483$, find $n$.
Find the sum of the odd integers between $10$ and $50$.
Find the sum: $$\frac17+\frac2{7^2}+\frac1{7^3}+\frac2{7^4}+\cdots$$
An infinite geometric series has first term $a$ and common ratio $r$. If the sum is $4$ and the second term is $\dfrac34$, find the possible value(s) for the common ratio $r$.
Find $b$ if $\dfrac12$, $a$, $b$, $8$, $c$ form an arithmetic sequence.

An office assistant fills a jar with $625$ jellybeans on Monday morning. Each day starting on Monday, one-fifth of the jellybeans get taken out of the jar and eaten. How many jellybeans are left at the end of Thursday?
Given the sequence $1, 2, 6, 13, 23, 36, \dots$. Let $D_1=2-1$, $D_2=6-2$, $D_3=13-6$, $D_4=23-13$, $\dots$. Find $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{20}D_n$.
What is the minimum $n$ such that the sum of the first $n$ terms of $-5, -1, 3, \dots$ will be at least $400$?
Evaluate: $$\sum_{a=1}^{3}\left[3a+\sum_{b=1}^{3}\left(3b+\sum_{c=1}^{3}3c\right)\right]$$
Find the sum of all positive 3-digit numbers that are divisible by $7$.

A ball is thrown from ground level up in the air to a height of $100$ yards. It then drops to the ground, and rebounds on each bounce four-fifths of the distance from which it fell. How far (in yards) does the ball travel before coming to rest?
What's the difference between $\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{n}(2k+1)$ and $\left(\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{n}2k\right)+1$? Subtract and simplify.
The sum of the first $k$ terms of the arithmetic sequence $-3, 2, 7, \dots$ is $116$. Find $k$.
